about: bank 0 $B0E4-$B8A5: the rebel training manual of the attract mode (page set-up, script runner, view), the shift library, math box helpers and sine table, bcd and random helpers, the score routines and their table, the site and cockpit view, the laser splash builder

B0:B0E4.name: manual_page_init
B0:B0E4.desc: starts one page of the rebel training manual, called by PHINXT. turns all messages off, calls the set-up routine of section Q_FRC (0 probot, 1 walkers, 2 TIE fighter, 3 asteroids) from manual_init_tab, then points the script pointer $4CB6 at the script of that section's page $4CB5, taken from manual_script_tab

B0:B111.name: man_init_probot
B0:B111.desc: manual set-up for section 0, the probot pages. sets the player's height to $0200, steps the page number $4CB5 on (0, 1, 2, then 0 again - this is the only place the page changes, so each pass through the four sections shows the next page of all of them), sets the demo probot up for that page (page 2 P2_86C7) and clears the transmission records (page 3 P3_98D3)

B0:B12E.name: man_init_walker
B0:B12E.desc: manual set-up for section 1, the walker pages. turns the player half round (-1.0 in the A.X and B.Y terms of the player's matrix), sets the height to $0800, sets the demo AT-ST up for page $4CB5 (page 1 P1_866F) and the demo AT-AT (page 0 P0_8674), then clears the AT-AT record's type byte so that only the AT-ST shows until the script calls man_show_atat

B0:B14E.name: man_show_atat
B0:B14E.desc: called from the walker scripts (command 5 records at time $65 on all three walker pages, after the AT-ST record has been cleared): raises the player to height $1800 and sets the demo AT-AT up again for page $4CB5 (page 0 P0_8674). reached only through the script, hence no caller found

B0:B15B.name: man_init_tie
B0:B15B.desc: manual set-up for section 2, the TIE fighter pages: B = page $4CB5, page 3 P3_8613 sets the alien records up

B0:B162.name: man_init_asteroid
B0:B162.desc: manual set-up for section 3, the asteroid pages: B = page $4CB5, page 2 P2_965E sets the demo asteroid up in the records at ALIENZ

B0:B189.name: manual_run
B0:B189.desc: the per-frame work of a manual page, called by the phase routine at L7542. if the time word of the script record at $4CB6 has been reached by PH_TIM it runs the record's command (byte 2, 0-6, through the table at LAE14, with U at the record: end of page, message on, message off, store byte, store word, call routine, nothing) and steps the pointer on 8 bytes - one record a frame at most. then it calls the move routine of section Q_FRC from manual_move_tab. the task text gives this as LB18A

B0:B1C5.name: man_move_probot
B0:B1C5.desc: per-frame movement for the probot pages of the manual: the probots (page 2 P2_877C), the gun shots (page 1 P1_9185) and the transmissions (page 3 P3_9989)

B0:B1CF.name: man_probot_fire
B0:B1CF.desc: called from the script of the probot weaponry page (command 5 record at $AE94, time $40): makes the demo probot, the first alien record, fire a shot (page 1 P1_9063, which with the manual flag $4CB9 set fires at once from the first gun record). reached only through the script, hence no caller found

B0:B1D6.name: man_probot_xmit
B0:B1D6.desc: called from the script of the probot weaponry page (command 5 record at $AEC4, time $B5): makes the demo probot launch a transmission (page 3 P3_98E8, which takes a free transmission record). reached only through the script, hence no caller found

B0:B1DD.name: man_move_walker
B0:B1DD.desc: per-frame movement for the walker pages of the manual: the AT-STs (page 1 P1_86E1), the AT-ATs (page 0 P0_8705) and the gun shots (page 1 P1_9185)

B0:B1E7.name: man_atst_fire
B0:B1E7.desc: called from the script of the AT-ST weaponry page (command 5 record at $AF6C, time $30): makes the demo AT-ST, the first record at $4A54, fire a shot (page 1 P1_8FF7). reached only through the script, hence no caller found

B0:B1EE.name: man_atat_fire
B0:B1EE.desc: called from the script of the AT-AT weaponry part of the same page (command 5 record at $AFA4, time $90): makes the demo AT-AT, the first record at $4A87, fire a shot (page 1 P1_8F8B). reached only through the script, hence no caller found

B0:B1F5.name: man_move_tie
B0:B1F5.desc: per-frame movement for the TIE fighter pages of the manual: the computer drones (page 3 CPU) and the gun shots (page 1 P1_9185)

B0:B1FC.name: man_tie_fire
B0:B1FC.desc: called from the script of the TIE fighter weaponry page (command 5 record at $B04C, time $55): makes the demo TIE fighter, the first alien record, fire a shot from the first gun record (page 1 P1_8F16, X = alien, U = gun). reached only through the script, hence no caller found

B0:B206.name: man_move_asteroid
B0:B206.desc: per-frame movement for the asteroid pages of the manual: page 2 P2_96E0 moves and launches the asteroids

B0:B20A.name: manual_view
B0:B20A.desc: draws a manual page, called by the view routine at LA697 with Y at the display list. turns on message $53 (REBEL TRAINING MANUAL   SECTION), views the messages, writes the section and page numbers after the heading as n.n, then calls the view routine of section Q_FRC from manual_view_tab

B0:B214.name: manual_view_num
B0:B214.desc: not a separate routine, the rest of manual_view (no call or jump to this address was found): colour, a move to the end of the heading, section number Q_FRC+1, a period, page number $4CB5+1, centre, then the section's view routine. the two upper-case comments here came over from a Star Wars routine with the same first instructions and do not describe this code

B0:B254.name: man_view_probot
B0:B254.desc: view routine of the probot pages: the transmissions (page 3 P3_9B6D) and the probots (page 2 P2_8FB7)

B0:B25B.name: man_view_walker
B0:B25B.desc: view routine of the walker pages: the AT-STs (page 1 P1_88FD) and the AT-ATs (page 0 P0_891A)

B0:B262.name: man_view_tie
B0:B262.desc: view routine of the TIE fighter pages: views the alien ships (page 3 SNVW_P3)

B0:B266.name: man_view_asteroid
B0:B266.desc: view routine of the asteroid pages: page 2 P2_9983 views the asteroid records. the upper-case comment on its line belongs to a Star Wars line and does not apply

B0:B2B1.name: asrd12
B0:B2B1.desc: arithmetic shift right of D by 12 bits, done as a byte move, sign extension and 4 shifts of B. first of five such entries (12 to 8 bits) that ESB puts in front of Atari's ASRD7-ASRD1 chain. no call to any of the five was found in either bank or the slapstic pages, they look like unused library code

B0:B2B9.name: asrd11
B0:B2B9.desc: arithmetic shift right of D by 11 bits: A to B, sign extend, 3 shifts of B. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B0:B2C0.name: asrd10
B0:B2C0.desc: arithmetic shift right of D by 10 bits: A to B, sign extend, 2 shifts of B. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B0:B2C6.name: asrd9
B0:B2C6.desc: arithmetic shift right of D by 9 bits: A to B, sign extend, 1 shift of B. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B0:B2CB.name: asrd8
B0:B2CB.desc: arithmetic shift right of D by 8 bits: A to B and sign extend. replaces the Star Wars ASRD8, which shifted eight times and fell into ASRD7. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B0:B2CF.desc: entry point: arithmetic shift D right 7 bits (falls through ASRD6..ASRD1 to the RTS at ASRD0)

B0:B2D9.desc: entry point: arithmetic shift D right 2 bits (falls through ASRD1 to the RTS at ASRD0)

B0:B2DB.desc: entry point: arithmetic shift D right 1 bit, then the RTS at ASRD0

B0:B2DE.name: lsrd12
B0:B2DE.desc: logical shift right of D by 12 bits: A to B, clear A, 4 shifts of B. first of a logical shift right library that Star Wars does not have: 12 to 8 bits as separate short routines, then a fall-through chain for 7 to 1 bits that starts in the bytes at LB2FC. only the 4 bit entry lsrd4 is called. no caller found for this one

B0:B2E6.name: lsrd11
B0:B2E6.desc: logical shift right of D by 11 bits: A to B, clear A, 3 shifts of B. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B0:B2ED.name: lsrd10
B0:B2ED.desc: logical shift right of D by 10 bits: A to B, clear A, 2 shifts of B. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B0:B2F3.name: lsrd9
B0:B2F3.desc: logical shift right of D by 9 bits: A to B, clear A, 1 shift of B. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B0:B2F8.name: lsrd8
B0:B2F8.desc: logical shift right of D by 8 bits: A to B, clear A. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B0:B302.name: lsrd4
B0:B302.desc: logical shift right of D by 4 bits, the one used entry of the logical shift chain (the 7, 6 and 5 bit entries are the six bytes in front of it, shown as data). called by the AT-AT view code in slapstic page 0 to turn a clamped distance into a brightness byte

B0:B30B.name: lsld12
B0:B30B.desc: shift D left 12 bits: B to A, clear B, 4 shifts of A. first of five such entries (12 to 8 bits) that ESB puts in front of Atari's LSLD7-LSLD1 chain. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B0:B313.name: lsld11
B0:B313.desc: shift D left 11 bits: B to A, clear B, 3 shifts of A. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B0:B31A.name: lsld10
B0:B31A.desc: shift D left 10 bits: B to A, clear B, 2 shifts of A. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B0:B320.name: lsld9
B0:B320.desc: shift D left 9 bits: B to A, clear B, 1 shift of A. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B0:B325.name: lsld8
B0:B325.desc: shift D left 8 bits: B to A and clear B. replaces the Star Wars LSLD8, which shifted eight times and fell into LSLD7. no caller found, unused as far as can be seen

B0:B331.desc: entry point: shift D left 3 bits (falls through LSLD2, LSLD1 to the RTS at LSLD0)

B0:B365.name: tranu1_entry
B0:B365.desc: the real entry of ESB's TRANU1: it saves U, which the transpose uses as its second scratch register, and the code ends with PULS U,PC where Star Wars has RTS. the TRANU1 label two bytes further on marks the part that matches Star Wars and must not be called by itself. no call to either address was found in bank 0, so the routine looks unused here

B0:B38D.name: store_u1_block
B0:B38D.desc: copies the ship 1 download block of the math box ($5028-$5045: the nine matrix terms, the three spare words and the position) into the unit vector block whose middle U points at - the reverse of the download IS1UV starts. called by slapstic page 0 P0_95C3 with U = M_AL

B0:B3F1.name: presub_via_u2
B0:B3F1.desc: runs the math box pre-subtract MS_PSB2 with ship 2's download block in the place of ship 1's: swaps the two blocks, starts program $67 for the block index the caller left in M_BIC and waits, then swaps the blocks back. called by the walker code in slapstic pages 0 and 1

B0:B3FD.name: swap_u1_u2
B0:B3FD.desc: exchanges the ship 1 download block ($5028-$5045) with the ship 2 block ($5048-$5065) word by word: the nine matrix terms and the position, not the three spare words. U is saved and used as the second scratch register. the three headers that follow are parts of this one routine

B0:B40B.name: swap_u1_u2_b
B0:B40B.desc: not a separate routine: swap_u1_u2 continues here with the A.Y word. no call or jump to this address was found

B0:B453.name: swap_u1_u2_c
B0:B453.desc: not a separate routine: swap_u1_u2 continues here with the C.Y word. no call or jump to this address was found

B0:B46B.name: swap_u1_u2_d
B0:B46B.desc: not a separate routine: swap_u1_u2 ends here with the three position words and PULS U,PC. no call or jump to this address was found

B0:B4B2.name: roll_by_angle
B0:B4B2.desc: rolls a unit vector block by an angle: B = angle (256 to the full turn), block index already in M_BIC. sets M_SIN and M_COS from the sine table and runs math box program MS_ROLL, waiting for it

B0:B4BA.name: pitch_by_angle
B0:B4BA.desc: pitches a unit vector block by an angle: B = angle (256 to the full turn), block index already in M_BIC. sets M_SIN and M_COS from the sine table and runs math box program MS_PTCH, waiting for it

B0:B4C2.name: yaw_by_angle
B0:B4C2.desc: yaws a unit vector block by an angle: B = angle (256 to the full turn), block index already in M_BIC. sets M_SIN and M_COS from the sine table and runs math box program MS_YAW, waiting for it. the most used of the three, called from all the enemy view code in the slapstic pages

B0:B4CA.name: set_sin_cos
B0:B4CA.desc: B = angle (256 to the full turn): writes its sine to M_SIN and its cosine to M_COS for the math box rotate programs. the cosine is the sine of the angle plus $40. X is saved, D returns the cosine

B0:B4E2.name: sine
B0:B4E2.desc: B = angle (256 to the full turn), returns D = sine as a signed fraction with $4000 = 1.0. looks the first quadrant up in the 65-word table sine_tab, reads the table backwards for the second quadrant and negates the value for angles $80-$FF. uses X

B0:B5C5.name: rnd_set
B0:B5C5.desc: ESB's form of the Star Wars RND8 (random number set): moves RND_S1 and RND_S2 down to RND_S3 and the byte after it, then reads two new bytes from the pokey random register P_RND1 into RND_S2 and RND_S1. called all over the slapstic pages before a routine that wants random bytes

B0:B5D4.name: scr_level_bonus
B0:B5D4.desc: adds the bonus for the level the game was started at, called once at frame $40 of the wave completed phase when $4C62 is set. GM_DIF 0 (easy) adds nothing, 1 adds 100000, 2 adds 250000 (the table at $B724, messages $4F-$51), 3 and up (continued play, message $52) adds the 8-digit bcd bonus carried over at $4BEF and shows it as the amount being added

B0:B61A.name: scr_legs_bonus
B0:B61A.desc: the progressive bonus for flying through an AT-AT's legs, called by slapstic page 0 P0_87DD when the player passes under a walker. adds 5000 to the 3-byte bcd bonus at $4CBF unless it has reached 900000, adds the bonus to the score, starts the 20-frame display timer $4CDF and a sound (LC657)

B0:B64E.name: scr_shot_3
B0:B64E.desc: score 3 points: an enemy shot destroyed by the player's laser, for a shot whose type byte has bit 6 clear (slapstic page 1 P1_92E8 and PTHTBG)

B0:B653.name: scr_shot_7
B0:B653.desc: score 7 points: an enemy shot destroyed by the player's laser, for a shot whose type byte has bit 6 set, as the AT-AT's shots have (slapstic page 1 P1_92E3 and PTHTBG)

B0:B658.name: scr_xmit_5
B0:B658.desc: score 5 points: called by slapstic page 3 P3_9CF2 when the laser hits a probot transmission record

B0:B65D.name: scr_wave_done
B0:B65D.desc: score 2500 points for completing a wave (message $4E, WAVE COMPLETED: 2,500 POINTS), called when the wave completed phase starts at L723E

B0:B662.name: scr_jedi
B0:B662.desc: score 20000 points: called by slapstic page 1 P1_95E8 when the letter bits at $4C80 reach $0F, all four letters of JEDI

B0:B667.name: scr_probot_25
B0:B667.desc: score 25 points for a probot shot down while the kill counter $4C53 is not yet zero (slapstic page 2 P2_92EE)

B0:B66C.name: scr_probot_250
B0:B66C.desc: score 250 points for a probot shot down once the kill counter $4C53 has run out (slapstic page 2 P2_92EE)

B0:B671.name: scr_probot_quota
B0:B671.desc: score 5000 points when a probot kill brings the counter $4C53 down to zero (slapstic page 2 P2_9341, which then calls the letter award on page 1)

B0:B676.name: scr_atst_50
B0:B676.desc: score 50 points for an AT-ST destroyed while the kill counter $4C53 is not yet zero (slapstic page 1 P1_8E33)

B0:B67B.name: scr_atst_500
B0:B67B.desc: score 500 points for an AT-ST destroyed once the kill counter $4C53 has run out (slapstic page 1 P1_8E33)

B0:B680.name: scr_atat_75
B0:B680.desc: score 75 points for an AT-AT destroyed, by laser or by tow cable, while the kill counter $4C53 is not yet zero (slapstic page 0 P0_9034 and P0_90C1)

B0:B685.name: scr_atat_750
B0:B685.desc: score 750 points for an AT-AT destroyed once the kill counter $4C53 has run out (slapstic page 0 P0_9047 and P0_90D4)

B0:B68A.name: scr_walker_quota
B0:B68A.desc: score 5000 points when a walker kill, AT-ST or AT-AT, brings the counter $4C53 down to zero (slapstic pages 0 and 1, which then call the letter award on page 1)

B0:B68F.name: scr_tie_100
B0:B68F.desc: score 100 points for a TIE fighter destroyed while the kill counter $4C53 is not yet zero (XPSA in slapstic page 3)

B0:B694.name: scr_tie_1000
B0:B694.desc: score 1000 points for a TIE fighter destroyed once the kill counter $4C53 has run out (XPSA in slapstic page 3)

B0:B699.name: scr_tie_quota
B0:B699.desc: score 5000 points when a TIE fighter kill brings the counter $4C53 down to zero (XPSA in slapstic page 3). four more routines of the same shape follow in the bytes at LB69E, shown as data and not called

B0:B74B.name: view_cockpit
B0:B74B.desc: draws the parts of the player's craft that show on the screen, ESB's replacement for the body of Star Wars VWPLAN, called by VWSITE and VWSITC with Y at the display list. takes the list for craft type $4C60 (0 or 1) from cockpit_lists and calls the four routines it names in turn: x shift, y shift, write the two positions, write colour and pictures. each list ends with the two picture words, which the fourth routine reads through X

B0:B77F.name: cockpit_no_x
B0:B77F.desc: first step of the cockpit list for craft type 1: no sideways shift, U = 0 and LZ_GX = 0. reached through cockpit_list_1, hence no caller found

B0:B786.name: cockpit_shift_y
B0:B786.desc: second step of both cockpit lists: the up and down shift of the cockpit from the site's screen y, as in Star Wars VWPLAN (whose comments it carries). stores it in LZ_GY and returns it in D as the y word of a position vector. reached through the lists, hence no caller found

B0:B79C.name: cockpit_put_pos
B0:B79C.desc: third step of both cockpit lists: writes the position vector, D = y word and U = x word, at 0,Y and again at 8,Y - one for each of the two pictures. reached through the lists, hence no caller found

B0:B7A5.name: cockpit_colour
B0:B7A5.desc: returns in D the display list word that colours the cockpit: JSRL $002A, the colour word kept in vector RAM, while the Jedi timer $4C50 runs or the flag $4C84 is set, else colour 1 at brightness $80. called by the two routines that follow

B0:B7B8.name: cockpit_put_2
B0:B7B8.desc: writes colour and picture for both parts of the cockpit: the colour word at 12,Y and the list's first picture word at 14,Y, then falls into cockpit_put_1 for the colour at 4,Y and the second picture word at 6,Y. X points at the picture words and is stepped past them

B0:B7C0.name: cockpit_put_1
B0:B7C0.desc: writes the colour word at 4,Y and the next picture word from X at 6,Y. the tail of cockpit_put_2 and the body of cockpit_one_part

B0:B7C9.name: cockpit_two_parts
B0:B7C9.desc: fourth step of both cockpit lists: writes colours and pictures for the two parts and moves Y past the 16 bytes built. reached through the lists, hence no caller found

B0:B7CF.name: cockpit_one_part
B0:B7CF.desc: a fourth step for a cockpit with one part: one colour and picture, Y moved on 8 bytes. neither list names it and no call was found, so it is unused

comments.B0:B0E7: section of the manual, 0-3: probot, walkers, TIE fighter, asteroids

comments.B0:B136: player height for the AT-ST part of the walker pages
comments.B0:B13C: B = page: the demo AT-ST goes in the first record at $4A54

comments.B0:B3F4: MS_PSB2, the 15-bit pre-subtract, for the block index in M_BIC

comments.B0:B6B4: ESB passes the address of the three bcd bytes in D, where Star Wars passed it in U
comments.B0:B6D4: a 6-digit amount: clear the top two digits of the amount shown

comments.B0:B763: this one reads the two picture words through X
comments.B0:B7AF: JSRL $002A: the colour word kept in vector RAM
comments.B0:B7BC: first picture word of the list
comments.B0:B7C4: second picture word of the list
comments.B0:B7D4: cockpit_lists: the list for craft type 0, then for type 1. each list is four routine addresses and two JSRL words to vector ROM pictures

4CB5.name: man_page
4CB5.desc: rebel training manual: page within the section, 0-2, shown as 1-3. stepped on by man_init_probot, so it changes once in every pass through the four sections

4CB6.name: man_script
4CB6.desc: rebel training manual: word, pointer to the next 8-byte record of the page's script (time word, command byte, operands). set by manual_page_init, stepped by manual_run

4A54.name: xmit_atst
4A54.desc: enemy record area with a different use in each wave: the three $28-byte probot transmission records ($4A54-$4ACB) in the probot wave, the AT-ST records of $11 bytes ($4A54-$4A86) in the walker wave. byte 0 of a record is zero when it is free

4A87.name: atat_rec
4A87.desc: start of the AT-AT walker records, $19 bytes each up to $4AD2 (slapstic page 0). byte 0 of a record is zero when it is free - man_init_walker clears the first one's

4BEF.name: cont_bonus
4BEF.desc: four bcd bytes, high first ($4BEF-$4BF2): the bonus for continued play, the score copied from $4BF4-$4BF7 at game over when $4C85 is set. shown on the wave select screen and with message $52, added to the score by scr_level_bonus when GM_DIF is 3 or more

4CBA.name: sc_add_hi
4CBA.desc: top two bcd digits of the amount being added to the score, the byte in front of SC_ADD - the amount is shown as 8 digits from here. zero except for the continued play bonus

4CBF.name: legs_bonus
4CBF.desc: three bcd bytes ($4CBF-$4CC1): the progressive bonus for flying through AT-AT legs. cleared when the walker wave starts, raised by 5000 and added to the score by scr_legs_bonus, shown while legs_bon_tmr runs

4CDF.name: legs_bon_tmr

4C84.name: jedi_glow
